literal: To goodness entitled who if asked, fearful water in the world, to others she who belongs shoulder those who do not touch.
translation: If asked who in this sea-girt world is entitled to true goodness, it is those who do not embrace the shoulders of another man's wife.
modern: அச்சம் தரும் கடலால் சூழப்பட்ட இவ்வுலகில் நன்மைகளுக்கு உரியவர்கள் யார் என்றால், பிறருக்கு உரியவளின் தோள்களைத் தழுவாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: The couplet asks a rhetorical question about who truly deserves goodness and virtue in this vast world. The answer is those who strictly refrain from touching the shoulders of a woman who belongs to another. The phrase 'fearful water' (நாமநீர்) refers to the awe-inspiring ocean that surrounds the earth, emphasizing the vastness of the world in contrast to the strict, intimate moral boundary of not desiring another's wife.
